regimens.dose_text: Target maintenance: 2 to 3 mg/kg daily orally (usually 100 to 200 mg daily). Initiate at 50 mg/day and titrate based on CBC and liver function. Onset of clinical immunosuppressive effect typically requires 6 to 12 months.

The initial dose is usually 3 to 5 mg/kg daily, beginning at the time of transplant. IMURAN is usually given as a single daily dose on the day of, and in a minority of cases 1 to 3 days before, transplantation.

dose.frequency: once daily (3 to 5 mg/kg/day starting at time of transplant)

regimens.dose_text: Initial dose: 3 to 5 mg/kg orally once daily beginning on the day of transplantation (or 1 to 3 days prior in select cases). Reduce dose in oliguric patients or TPMT/NUDT15 deficiency.

regimens.indication: Prevention of Rejection in Renal Homotransplantation — Maintenance

refs.quote: Renal Homotransplantation: IMURAN is indicated as an adjunct for the prevention of rejection in renal homotransplantation.
Dose reduction to maintenance levels of 1 to 3 mg/kg daily is usually possible. The dose of IMURAN should not be increased to toxic levels because of threatened rejection.

regimens.dose_text: Maintenance dose: 1 to 3 mg/kg orally once daily. Do not increase to toxic levels because of threatened rejection; discontinue if severe hematologic or other toxicity develops.

refs.quote: Rheumatoid Arthritis: IMURAN is indicated for the treatment of active rheumatoid arthritis (RA) to reduce signs and symptoms.

The initial dose should be approximately 1.0 mg/kg (50 to 100 mg) given as a single dose or on a twice-daily schedule. The dose may be increased, beginning at 6 to 8 weeks and thereafter by steps at 4-week intervals, if there are no serious toxicities and if initial response is unsatisfactory. Dose increments should be 0.5 mg/kg daily, up to a maximum dose of 2.5 mg/kg per day.

dose.frequency: once daily or in two divided doses; titrate by 0.5 mg/kg/day up to 2.5 mg/kg/day

regimens.dose_text: Initial: ~1.0 mg/kg (50 to 100 mg) orally once daily or in 2 divided doses. Increase by 0.5 mg/kg/day at 6–8 weeks and every 4 weeks thereafter if needed, up to max 2.5 mg/kg/day. Minimum adequate trial is 12 weeks; taper by 0.5 mg/kg (~25 mg/day) q4wk to lowest effective maintenance dose.

The use of IMURAN in nursing mothers is not recommended. Azathioprine or its metabolites are transferred at low levels, both transplacentally and in breast milk. 8, 9, 10 Because of the potential for tumorigenicity shown for azathioprine, a decision should be made whether to discontinue nursing or discontinue the drug, taking into account the importance of the drug to the mother.
